title: Method of Early Diagnosis of Abnormal Movements of Patients with Tremor Symptoms Using Augmented Reality
content: According to WHO estimates, neurological disorders cause approximately 11 million deaths annually worldwide, with late diagnosis representing a critical contributing factor. We present a novel augmented reality (AR)-based method for improving the accuracy and early detection of tremor as a key symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD) and neurological disorders caused by traumatic brain injury (TBI). Unlike conventional drawing tests, the proposed approach eliminates physical surface contact, removing the compensatory motor anchor that allows patients to mask subtle tremor manifestations. The method was validated in 131 participants: 50 healthy controls, 6 PD patients, and 75 combat veterans with TBI, and compared against the standard geometric figure drawing test. The standard test failed to detect tremor in 2 of 6 PD patients (33%), whereas the AR method identified it in all 6 patients (100%). In the TBI group, the AR test revealed tremor in 3 of 75 participants who passed the standard test undetected. A baseline classifier confirmed higher sensitivity for the AR approach across both clinical groups. These results support the potential of AR-based tremor assessment as an early neurodiagnostic tool, particularly for combat-related TBI – a population that has not previously been addressed in AR diagnostic research. Future work will focus on scaling the dataset and implementing a deep learning classifier.
